Hero Names and Costumes.text: A hero name is the name a pro works under, and Hero Course students choose theirs during their first year as part of their training. A name should say what kind of hero someone means to be; a teacher can send back one that is embarrassing, misleading or already taken, and it becomes official when the Hero Public Safety Commission registers it with a license. Until then students go by their own names. Hero costumes are designed by the hero and built by support companies: every Hero Course student files a costume request with measurements, Quirk details and sketches on enrollment, and U.A.'s partner companies deliver the finished costumes in numbered cases. A costume is protective gear first and an image second: fabric suited to the Quirk, armor where the body takes impact, built-in support items, and colors the public will remember. Changes go through the Development Studio or the original company, and Support Course students compete for the work. Licensed heroes own their costumes, register any support item that could serve as a weapon, and pay to replace what villains wreck. A costume licenses nobody: a costumed person using a Quirk in public without a license is a vigilante in the eyes of the law.
